A new theoretical framework, incorporating the kinetic effects of a finite thickness of current layers, has been developed to analyze the stability of microtearing modes and other similar instabilities. This model stands in contrast to previous theories that treated these modes as being mode-mode magnetic island coalescence. Current-layer width-dependent magnetic island dynamics are a hallmark of the microtearing mode and other similar modes. The outcome of our analysis shows that modes involving coalescing islands are universally unstable above a certain critical surface layer thickness. This is in line with previous findings for tearing modes. Furthermore, our results reveal that magnetic reconnection can effectively widen islands, thus creating a feedback loop that could lead to an instability in the microtearing mode and other such modes.

A new challenge in the computer vision field, known as fashion attribute manipulation, is explored in this paper. Fashion attribute manipulation involves the ability to alter specific visual characteristics of clothing items within images, a task crucial for enhancing image search and retrieval tasks in real-world applications. Current research in image editing primarily focuses on manipulating a single image, but our work introduces a new dual-image editing challenge, referred to as fashion attribute transfer, a critical step towards more complex manipulation tasks. A comprehensive dataset of 128,000 high-quality fashion images was compiled to develop a more robust fashion attribute editor, and our system outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in both accuracy and generalizability.

An iterative method is developed to address ill-posed problems that have a smooth solution by utilizing an O-source as a regularizer. The method incorporates a variational inequality to derive a source functional and can be interpreted as a Landweber iteration with a non-linear, scale-invariant smoothing effect when a convex but unbounded regularizer is used. This method is particularly suitable for problems described by an operator equation with a strongly convex but unbounded function as a constraint. Convergence rates are proven both theoretically and numerically with appropriate choice of stopping criterion.

Achieving precise depth perception from light field images presents significant challenges due to the limited data available per pixel and the depth ambiguity inherent in these multi-view images. In an attempt to overcome these obstacles, researchers have developed an efficient method for estimating depth in affine light field images. The approach utilizes a basic and swift cost constructor to produce reliable depth predictions, while a learning-based refiner enhances depth resolution without imposing significant computational demands. The proposed technique surpasses existing techniques for light field depth estimation, offering reliable depth estimates even in cases where objects exhibit complex textures.

This study uses the bilinear method to investigate the Fokas-Lenells equations, first reducing the system and then exploring both nonlinear wave and rational solutions. We find and present the one- and two-soliton solutions, as well as the highest-order soliton solutions, of the coupled Fokas-Lenells equations. We demonstrate the validity of these solutions and derive a novel oscillatory rational solution, which has significant implications for the analysis of the local M\"obius transformations on the phase space of the Dirac system.

Alternative theories of gravity that go beyond the Riemannian framework have been explored extensively but often risk running into difficulties with the variation principle due to their unusual properties. To address this issue, researchers employ double field theory, an innovative formalism rooted in the principles of string theory, allowing the construction of action-based descriptions for these unconventional theories. By leveraging this principle, scientists can develop novel examples of gravity theories that might be applicable in the context of cosmology.

To meet growing demands for next-generation Home WiFi networks, such as high-resolution video streaming and VR experiences, it is crucial to optimize both network performance and user satisfaction. By considering user satisfaction as a key metric, we define a problem of multi-objective network flow optimization to maximize user satisfaction while minimizing network delay. The proposed solution involves using deep reinforcement learning to find a practical heuristic, requiring no prior knowledge of the network environment. The approach models Home WiFi networks as Graph Neural Networks, uses the same architecture for training and inference, and leverages vector-based multi-objective reward functions. The proposed method demonstrates a 10-fold speed increase in user satisfaction compared to conventional solutions.
